objective.text: Build shapes and name them by their sides: triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Build, identify, and analyze two-dimensional shapes with specified attributes.

explanations.title: What a polygon is
explanations.text: A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides. It has 3 or more sides. It has as many angles as sides.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: polygon description

explanations.title: Word parts tell the number
explanations.text: Tri- means 3, so a triangle has 3 angles. Quad- means 4, so a quadrilateral has 4 sides.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: sentence strips (tri-, quad-, lateral)

explanations.title: Build it with sticks
explanations.text: Join 2 sticks to make an angle. Add 1 more stick to close it. Now you have a triangle.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: spaghetti triangle

explanations.title: Named by attributes
explanations.text: These quadrilaterals look different. They are all quadrilaterals because they all have 4 straight sides.

misconceptions.label: Calling an open shape a polygon
misconceptions.description: Child thinks a figure with a gap, or with only 2 sides, is a polygon.
detection_signals: Says yes when asked if an open figure is a polygon.
Says a polygon can have 2 angles or 2 sides.
misconceptions.response_text: A polygon must be closed. Every side meets 2 other sides. Add a side to close it.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'Is this a polygon? No! It's not closed!'

misconceptions.label: Naming by look instead of attributes
misconceptions.description: Child will not call a shape a quadrilateral (or triangle) because it does not look like the usual picture.
detection_signals: Says 'it is not a triangle' or 'I can't name it' for a shape with 3 or 4 sides.
Names a shape by size or tilt, not by side count.
misconceptions.response_text: Count the straight sides. 4 sides means it is a quadrilateral, even if it looks unusual.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'because of their shared attributes not because of the way they look'

assets_required.why_this_method: Side and angle counts must be exact. Diffusion often draws wrong numbers of sides.
assets_required.description: Draws one polygon (or open figure) from a list of corner points. Can mark each angle with a small arc and number the sides.
must_show_exactly: Number of sides and corners exactly equals the question stimulus
Straight sides only, unless the stimulus asks for a curve
Open figures show a clear gap
Open figure for q_pr_6 has exactly 2 sides meeting at 1 corner
